From [the documentation](https://docs.celeryproject.org/en/stable/userguide/tasks.html):

> ### How do I import the task decorator? And what’s “app”?
> The task decorator is available on your [`Celery`](https://docs.celeryproject.org/en/stable/reference/celery.html#celery.Celery) application instance, if you don’t know what this is then please read [First Steps with Celery](https://docs.celeryproject.org/en/stable/getting-started/first-steps-with-celery.html#first-steps).
>
> If you’re using Django (see [First steps with Django](https://docs.celeryproject.org/en/stable/django/first-steps-with-django.html#django-first-steps)), or you’re the author of a library then you probably want to use the `shared_task()` decorator:
>
> ```python
> from celery import shared_task
> @shared_task
> def add(x, y):
>     return x + y
> ```
